title: Campaign handoff: recombination findings, weak table decay, and execution-integrity reset
abstract: The recorded campaign tested systems-kernel, architecture, and memory-regularization directions. Fused n-gram hash construction was throughput-null, Canon convolution regressed quality, factorized n-gram codes failed their two-sided falsifier, and the AttnRes plus table-decay factorial revealed a super-additive negative interaction. Weak n-gram table decay produced a large preliminary benefit only in the five-shard diagnostic regime. No new GPU work is authorized in this reporting period because the local executable setup has drifted and the H200 SSH endpoint is not currently reachable.
methods: This synthesis reads the structured experiment, run-evidence, refinement-decision, and setup registries. It separates multi-seed evidence from single-seed pilots and keeps five-shard diagnostic results distinct from the active ten-shard wall-time decision frame. The historical runs were registered post hoc from a remote-SSH launcher and lack the active challenge tag required for top-level hourly-paper run references, so this report cites their structured evidence records while explicitly recording that provenance limitation. Startup validation, setup reconciliation checks, hourly-report status, local process inventory, and bounded SSH connectivity checks were also performed.

findings.statement: The byte-identical fused n-gram hash construction did not improve throughput across three paired seeds.
limitations: The evidence rejects the tested allocation-fusion diagnosis, not all n-gram kernel optimization.

findings.statement: The tested zero-initialized Canon depthwise convolution regressed endpoint validation BPB on all four paired seeds.
limitations: This verdict applies to the tested kernel size, learning rate, and integration point.

findings.statement: The backoff-gate diagnostic supports the premise that n-gram memorization harm concentrates in the lower-data regime, while remaining neutral at ten shards.
limitations: The helping result is a single-seed five-shard diagnostic and is not an adoption result in the active ten-shard frame.

findings.statement: Factorized n-gram codes failed both sides of their preregistered falsifier.
limitations: The result rejects the implemented paired-hash construction, not every possible factorized code.

findings.statement: AttnRes remains unresolved because its wall-time arm completed substantially fewer steps than control.
limitations: A fixed-step isolation test is required before separating architectural quality from naive-kernel cost.

findings.statement: AttnRes combined with strong n-gram table decay produced a super-additive negative interaction in the single-seed factorial.
limitations: The interaction is single-seed and both component settings are themselves non-adopted.

findings.statement: Weak n-gram table decay at 0.02 and 0.05 produced large preliminary five-shard improvements.
limitations: The result needs multi-seed confirmation and a ten-shard paired check before it can inform the active frame.

negative_results: B1 fused n-gram hash allocation was throughput-null.
A1 Canon convolution regressed validation BPB on four paired seeds.
C2 factorized n-gram codes failed at both five and ten shards.
Strong n-gram table decay at 0.2 regressed the ten-shard operating point.
The first AttnRes kernel-refinement attempt crashed because an in-place buffer invalidated autograd views.
limitations: The eight historical experiments were registered post hoc from an informal remote launcher, omit formal search-policy bindings, and cannot be treated as provenance-complete active-challenge runs.
Several findings use five-shard diagnostics outside the active ten-shard decision frame.
The local train.py bytes do not match the reconciliation record, the named baseline artifact is absent locally, and check-setup therefore blocks execution.
The supplied H200 SSH endpoint timed out during bounded connectivity checks, so GPU occupancy could not be verified.
decisions: Do not authorize new GPU work until the exact executable training code and baseline provenance are restored or re-measured and check-setup is green.
Reject the tested B1, A1, C2, and strong table-decay settings.
Keep AttnRes on hold pending a fixed-step mechanism-isolation test.
Promote weak table decay only to a current-scope ten-shard, multi-seed proposal after setup repair and novelty-gate completion.
Require the formal staged scheduler, challenge tags, physical-GPU binding, and complete ledger chain for all new runs.

next_hour_plan.question: Can the exact executable training tree and baseline provenance be restored and verified on the supplied H200 endpoint?
next_hour_plan.why_now: All effect work is invalid until the setup drift, missing artifact, and unreachable SSH path are resolved.
next_hour_plan.stop_condition: Stop and report a blocking failure if the endpoint remains unreachable or the reconciled baseline cannot be tied to exact code and artifacts; otherwise require validate, check-setup, audit, and GPU inventory to pass.

next_hour_plan.question: Does weak n-gram table decay improve the active ten-shard wall-time frame under fresh concurrent controls?
next_hour_plan.why_now: It is the strongest open mechanistic lead, but its observed benefit is currently confined to the five-shard diagnostic regime.
next_hour_plan.stop_condition: Stop the line if the first paired stage misses the preregistered endpoint and throughput boundaries; promote only through the unchanged 1-to-3-to-6-to-10 funnel.

next_hour_plan.question: Does AttnRes improve quality per update when control and treatment are matched at a fixed step count?
next_hour_plan.why_now: The existing wall-time result cannot separate architectural value from a 26 percent step-count penalty.
next_hour_plan.stop_condition: Reject the mechanism if fixed-step quality is null or worse; if positive, treat kernel fusion as a separate refinement rather than an effect conclusion.
